name: Jerimoth
overview: Jerimoth was a male Levite, specifically known as the son of Heman, who was set apart for prophetic ministry through music. He was chosen fifteenth by lot among the singers who prophesied with lyres, harps, and cymbals, highlighting his role in the worship practices of Israel. His ministry was closely connected to the Levitical tradition of musical praise and prophecy.
namesAndTitles: The name Jerimoth means 'swollen or obese' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but is recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:4. The meaning of the name is noted without additional theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Jerimoth is explicitly identified as the son of Heman, a notable figure in the Levitical line. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Jerimoth beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jerimoth's significance in Scripture lies in his role as a member of the Levitical singers dedicated to prophesying through music. Being chosen fifteenth by lot among these musicians indicates a divinely ordered participation in temple worship. His ministry exemplifies the God-ordained use of musical instruments and prophetic expression to lead Israel in worship, reflecting the importance of the Levites in spiritual leadership.
